## What We Did

<!-- CHANGE THIS: replace with your own notes -->

Set up the portfolio workflow: made a repository from a template, cloned it with GitHub Desktop, edited files in RStudio, rendered with Quarto, and published to GitHub Pages.


## Key Concepts

Three places a file can live:

1. **My computer** — where I edit
2. **GitHub.com** — where it's stored
3. **My live site** — what the world sees

The loop: **Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh**

## Proving R Works

The chunk below runs when this page renders. If you can see a result underneath
it on your published site, R and Quarto are talking to each other correctly.

```{r}
sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string
```

## Reflection

<!-- CHANGE THIS: 3-4 sentences -->

What I want out of this course: 

I have some experience accessing Census APIs, scraping open data portals, and running spatial joins, but I'd like to get more comfortable with these skills. I'm also looking forward to gaining experience with GIS and eventually using what I learn for modeling. 
My master's program has been great for building out technical skills but I haven't had as much in-class opportunity to apply the skills to real-world datasets or questions about public policy. I'm excited to learn more about how to responsibly investigate/examine policy choices across many domains. 

One thing I'm nervous about:

I don't have GIS experience yet. I feel confident I'll be able to pick it up but might be worse off starting out compared to MUSA students and other classmates with more experience.

One thing I learned on Friday:

I've used GitHub on a couple of projects before, but mostly from the command line / occasionally the browser; using the desktop app for ~the first time was more intuitive than I expected.
